paper_title: SeMo3D: Unifying 3D Generation, Editing, and Completion via Selective Modeling

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: 3D generation, editing, and completion are typically treated as regenerating the complete 3D asset under task-specific constraints, even when only a local region needs modification. This leads to task isolation, inconsistency in content that should remain unchanged, and dependence on task-specific paired data. We address these issues with a key observation: the three tasks all synthesize a designated region while keeping the rest intact---the full region for generation, the target region for editing, and the missing region for completion. We term this paradigm Selective Modeling and build SeMo3D upon it; it naturally unifies the three tasks, preserves unchanged content by construction, and enables training without paired editing or completion data, since any 3D asset can be partitioned into a selected region and its context. For training, we propose region-selective denoising, which randomly selects regions of varying sizes on standard 3D assets and applies noise and loss only to them, jointly learning all three tasks. For architecture, we propose Omni3DiT, a multi-condition 3D diffusion transformer that distinguishes regions to create from those to retain and fuses image, text, and point guidance for fine-grained control. Experiments across three benchmarks show SeMo3D surpasses state-of-the-art methods on all tasks, delivering multimodal controllability in generation and strong consistency and accuracy in editing and completion. SeMo3D further serves as a unified modeling tool for agents, enabling efficient 3D creation through natural-language interaction. Project page: https://xiaokunsun.github.io/SeMo3D.github.io/.

Project page: https://xiaokunsun.github.io/ SeMo3D.github.io/. 1 Figure 2. (a) Existing holistic modeling regenerates the complete asset even for local modification, requiring per-task models and paired editing/completion data, while regions that should remain unchanged are often altered (black boxes). (b) Our selective modeling synthesizes only the designated region, unifying the three tasks, preserving the rest by construction, and needing no task-specific paired data. 1. Introduction 3D content creationspanning generation [36, 40], editing [21], completion [84], and their combinationsis central to games [92], AR/VR [1, 44], robotics [12, 55], and digital twins [47]. Although typically studied in isolation, these tasks are conventionally viewed through the same lens: regenerating complete 3D asset under task-specific constraintsmatching the condition for generation, and additionally the source asset for editing or the partial input for completion. unified framework covering all three within one model is thus appealing yet remains an open problem. Driven by generative models [24, 41] and large-scale 3D datasets [13, 14], all three tasks have advanced rapidly. As illustrated in Fig. 2(a), mainstream feed-forward approaches [11, 56, 72, 7678] share common paradigm we term holistic modeling: creating the complete 3D asset under image or text guidance. To preserve consistency with the source, editing and completion methods [11, 56, 72, 76] additionally condition on the source asset or partial input, yet they still regenerate the entire object even when only local region needs to be modified.1 This creates fundamental mismatch between what needs to change and what is actually modeled, which leads to three key limitations. (1) Task isolation. As each task imposes different constraint, generation [77, 78, 94], editing [46, 72, 76], and 1In this paper, editing refers to local operations like addition, deletion, or replacement, not global operations like style transfer. completion [11, 25, 45] rely on separate models with distinct architectures and objectives, duplicating design and training effort across tasks and multiplying deployment costs. (2) Region inconsistency. Because the full asset is regenerated, source fidelity can only be encouraged rather than guaranteed, and regions that should remain intact are (3) Editfrequently altered (black boxes in Fig. 2(a)). ing/completion data dependency. Regenerating whole asset that respects the source demands sourcetarget supervision, so many editing [19, 72, 76, 93] and completion [11, 25, 45] methods require costly large-scale paired datasets (e.g., PartFlow [72] curates 100K editing pairs via seven-stage pipeline), limiting scalability. Moreover, most methods accept only single guidance modality (image or text), offering limited control: text lacks geometric precision, while images leave occluded regions ambiguous. Our key observation is that, despite their different constraints, the three tasks share common structure: synthesizing designated region while keeping the rest intact the full, target, and missing regions for generation, editing, and completion. This motivates selective modeling: given an asset represented by spatially aligned tokens (e.g., structured latents [77, 78]), the model synthesizes only the selected tokens and reuses the rest (Fig. 2(b)), unlike holistic modeling. Selective modeling thus (1) unifies the three tasks, which differ only in the selected region; (2) preserves unchanged content by construction, as context tokens are 2 never regenerated;2 and (3) requires no task-specific paired data, since any ordinary asset can be partitioned into selected region and its context. This resolves the three limitations above in single paradigm. Based on this insight, we present SeMo3D, multicondition model unifying 3D generation, editing, and completion via Selective Modeling, as illustrated in Fig. 1. We instantiate selective modeling through two key components. On the training side, we propose region-selective denoising: randomly selecting regions of varying sizes on ordinary 3D assets, adding noise only to the selected tokens, and denoising them while keeping the rest clean. As the selected region ranges from small portion to the full region, this single procedure spans the entire task spectrum, from local editing through partial completion to full generation, without task-specific paired supervision. On the architecture side, we design Omni3DiT, unified multicondition 3D diffusion transformer that jointly processes clean context and noisy selected tokens, and further fuses complementary image, text, and point conditions for finegrained control. Experiments on three benchmarks show that SeMo3D outperforms specialized state-of-the-art methods on all tasks, with flexible multi-condition control in generation and high-fidelity preservation in editing and completion. SeMo3D further supports agentic and interactive 3D modeling through natural-language interaction. Our contributions are summarized as follows: We formulate selective modeling, unified paradigm that casts 3D generation, editing, and completion as synthesizing the designated region while preserving the rest, and present SeMo3D to instantiate this paradigm. We introduce region-selective denoising, which learns all three tasks from standard 3D datasets alone, without costly large-scale paired editing or completion datasets. We develop Omni3DiT, multi-condition 3D diffusion transformer integrating clean 3D context with image, text, and point guidance for unified controllable 3D creation. 2. Related Work 3D Generation. Driven by 2D generative models [24, 41, 50, 54, 61, 62], 3D generation has undergone rapid paradigm shifts. Early methods [8, 51, 52, 59, 69] use score distillation sampling (SDS) to lift 2D priors to 3D, but suffer from long optimization times. Multi-view 2D methods [42, 43, 67, 73, 79] accelerate generation by first synthesizing multi-view images and then producing 3D shapes in feed-forward manner. More recently, native 3D generative models [20, 28, 32, 74, 77, 78, 86, 94, 95, 97] operating directly on 3D latents have pushed quality and scalability further. Despite this progress, most methods condition on 2In this paper, preservation by construction holds at the token level: context tokens stay exactly unchanged. Given the near-lossless reconstruction of structured latents [78], this virtually equals asset-level preservation. single modality (image or text), limiting fine-grained controllability. Recent efforts incorporate pairwise combinations such as image-text [7, 9] or image-point [29, 75], but none of the above jointly leverages all three modalities to combine the visual detail of images, the semantic expressiveness of text, and the geometric precision of points. 3D Editing and Completion. 3D editing and completion have evolved analogously: from SDS-based optimization [10, 27, 30, 37, 57, 100, 101] through multi-view 2D methods [3, 4, 16, 18, 35, 70] to native 3D approaches [11, 25, 45, 56, 72, 76]. Native 3D methods are training-free or training-based. Training-free methods [26, 31, 33, 82, 89, 99] repurpose pretrained generators via inversion or opthey largely maintain source consistency but timization; require slow, multi-step pipelines. Training-based methods [6, 11, 15, 19, 25, 45, 46, 56, 71, 72, 76, 80, 93] enable fast feed-forward inference but rely on large paired editing or completion datasets (e.g., 100K pairs in PartFlow [72], 116K in 3DEditFormer [76]) and often alter regions that should remain unchanged. Moreover, both lines mostly use single modality, limiting controllability. Unified 3D Multimodal Models. Recent works [85, 87, 88, 90, 91] consolidate multimodal output capabilities into one model, typically unifying 3D understanding with generation and editing [85, 88, 90, 91] or bridging 2D and 3D generation [87]. However, these models are largely built on VLM-based architectures, limiting their native 3D modeling capacity, and their notion of unity centers on merging different output modalities (e.g., text, image, and 3D) rather than different 3D creation sub-tasks (generation, editing, and completion). They also typically condition on only one or two modalities, and those that support editing still rely on large-scale paired editing supervision. Compared with all three lines of work above, SeMo3D offers distinct solution: it recasts 3D generation, editing, and completion as single selective-modeling problem formulated directly on native 3D representations, unifying the three tasks without task-specific architectures or per-task paired supervision while preserving the remaining content by construction. Additionally, SeMo3D supports joint image, text, and point conditioning, enhancing controllability. 3. Methodology 3.1. Preliminaries Structured Latents. Both embeddings are zeroinitialized to preserve pretrained behavior at initialization. Text Conditioning. Trellis2 conditions only on images via DINOv3 [60] cross-attention, yet images cannot describe occluded content. We add parallel cross-attention text branch [7, 9] injecting CLIP [53] features. Both branches share one query and sum their outputs into residual stream. The text branch output projection is zero-initialized, leaving the pretrained pathway initially undisturbed. Point Conditioning. Image and text provide rich visual and semantic guidance but cannot specify exact 3D locations. We therefore add points as third condition, using sparse rather than dense points since they make user interaction far easier. In the SS stage, each point is represented by shared learnable embedding, positioned via RoPE [64] at its voxel coordinate, and concatenated into the token sequence [34]. Since points share the 3D space of latent tokens, self-attention enables direct spatial reasoning between points and latent tokens, proving substantially more effective than point cross-attention (Sec. 4.3). The SLat stages omit point conditioning, as image and text suffice for geometry and texture once the sparse structure is determined. Compositional Condition Dropout. Naively finetuning with all conditions active risks letting the pretrained image branch dominate, suppressing the newly added text and point pathways. At each training step, random subset of modalities is kept active while the rest are replaced with null embeddings. Conclusion We present SeMo3D, unified framework that casts 3D generation, editing, and completion as selective modeling synthesizing only the designated region while preserving the rest. Around this core idea, we design region-selective denoising and Omni3DiT, enabling one model to handle all three tasks without task-specific paired data while accepting complementary image, text, and point guidance. Experiments show that SeMo3D surpasses specialized stateof-the-art methods across all three tasks. Agent integration further enables an intuitive, efficient 3D creation workflow. Limitations and Future Work. SeMo3D inherits Trellis2s structured latents [78], whose limited resolution cannot capture very fine structures such as thin palm fronds (Fig. 10, top); higher-fidelity 3D representations [38, 58, 65] could alleviate this. Moreover, the CLIP [53] text encoder struggles with complex compositional prompts: the orange fruits are reduced to orange texture rather than generated as objects (Fig. 10, bottom); stronger visionlanguage encoders [2, 83] are promising remedy. 6. sections.title: Supplementary Material
sections.content: This supplementary material provides training details (Sec. 7), experimental details (Sec. 8), robustness analysis (Sec. 9), and additional results (Sec. 10). 7. Training Details Training Data. We train on the training split of Trellis500K [77], filtering out assets with an aesthetic score below 4.5. Each sample pairs one asset with randomly chosen rendered view as the image condition and randomly chosen dataset caption as the text condition. No paired editing or completion data is used. Point Conditions. Points lie on the 163 SS grid, with at most 32 per sample. During training, we first use farthest point sampling (FPS) to obtain 32 spatially distributed points from occupied voxels inside S, then draw uniformly from 1 to 32 and randomly select of these points; unused slots are filled with masked padding tokens. This random subsampling improves robustness to variations in the number and spatial distribution of user-provided point conditions (Sec. 9). Hyperparameters. All three stages are initialized from Trellis2 [78], with settings listed in Tab. 5. We use AdamW with learning rate of 5105, weight decay of 0.01, an EMA rate of 0.9999, and bfloat16 mixed precision. Region-Selective Denoising. Full-region and local-region In the localmodes are sampled with equal probability. region mode, we sample 3D box with random side lengths (Tab. 5) and position, restricted to the half of the asset facing the condition camera so that the selected region is observed by the image. Sparse boxes are rejected, and accepted ones are shrunk to fit their occupied voxels. The SS grid has resolution =16; at inference, its partition is transferred to the 323 SLat grid by nearest-neighbor upsampling. Compositional Condition Dropout. Each step keeps one condition combination and nulls the rest. For the SS stage, {I, T, P}, {I, T}, and {I, P} are each sampled with probability 0.2, and {I}, {T}, {P}, and with 0.1 each. For the SLat stages, {I, T}, {I}, {T}, and are sampled with probabilities 0.5, 0.2, 0.2, and 0.1, respectively. The image is thus withheld in 30% of steps, and trains the unconditional branch for classifier-free guidance [23]. In the standard CFG dropout ablation, each stage retains all available conditions with probability 0.9 and drops them all with probability 0.1: the SS stage uses only {I, T, P} or , and the SLat stages use only {I, T} or . Experimental Details 8.1. Benchmarks and Metrics Generation. We use the Toys4K [63] test split of Trellis500K, which is disjoint from the training split, keeping the 3,180 objects with text annotations (105 categories). Each object comes with one condition image and one caption, and its point condition consists of 32 points sampled by FPS from the assets occupancy. Generated and ground-truth meshes are rendered from 8 views at 15 elevation with 45 azimuth spacing. LPIPS [96] and DINOv2 [49] similarity are averaged over view-aligned render pairs, while FID [22] and KID [5] compare the two render sets using Inception-v3 features [66]. CD uses 10K surface points per mesh, with each mesh normalized to unit box. Editing. Edit3D-Bench [33] contains 300 editing cases, each with source asset, 3D edit region, an edited image, and text prompt. Edited and source assets are rendered from 16 views at 15 and 30 elevations. Consistency is measured outside the edit region: PSNR, SSIM [68], and LPIPS on unmasked pixels of view-aligned renders, and CD on 20K surface points with those inside the edit region removed. Quality is measured by FID between source and edited renders and by FVD between their 120-frame orbit videos. Accuracy is measured on 6 frontal views by DINOv2 similarity to the edited image and CLIP [53] similarity to the prompt. Completion. Omni-Comp [82] contains 180 partial inputs created by single-view scanning, part removal, and random cropping. For SeMo3D, the point condition consists of 32 points sampled by FPS from ground-truth surface points farther than 0.02 from the partial input. The no-point variant uses the same image and text conditions without these additional points. We sample 16K points from both the completed mesh and the ground truth, and apply the same normalization transform to both so that they remain aligned in shared coordinate system. Robustness Mask Size. User-specified masks are rarely tight, so we enlarge each Edit3D-Bench edit region by up to 40% about its center. As shown in Fig. 12, SeMo3D yields nearly identical edits across all sizes, without adding spurious geometry. Since the SS stage decides occupancy within S, looser mask does not force content into it. Number of Condition Points. We vary the number of condition points across 16, 32, and 48, while keeping the image and text conditions fixed. As shown in Fig. 13, the generated assets retain consistent overall geometry across all three counts. The 48-point results further show generalization beyond the training maximum of 32 points. Spatial Distribution of Condition Points. We also compare three spatial distributions of condition points for each asset, keeping the image and text conditions fixed. As shown in Fig. 14, SeMo3D preserves the overall structure of the mecha and tricycle across these distributions, while local geometry and appearance may vary. Together, these results indicate robustness to variations in both the number and spatial distribution of point conditions. 10. Additional Results Agentic Interactive 3D Modeling.
